title: Head Height
summary: A whole day with no Contact in it. The party are handed municipal grey paint and a docket for twelve walls, and everything they learn costs them walls. A public information meeting, a lawyer who is angry on his daughter's behalf, a doctor who asks the only question that matters and then leaves, and a dog that will not walk on one particular piece of pavement.
structure: Four quarters, one continuous day, no combat by design. Morning is an investigation on a visible clock; noon is a set-piece conversation the party attend as scenery; evening is the scheduling game biting for the first time; night is a forty-second scene that should be the thing they remember.
designRequirement: Nothing in this episode resolves. It ends with a map, a document that contradicts itself, a lead they did not have time for, and one person at the table who saw something the others did not.
castingNote: Two of the three set-piece NPCs are sympathetic and the third is a man complaining about a spaniel. If it plays grim, something has gone wrong — Kudo is angry, not bleak, and being angry on behalf of someone you love is a warm thing to watch.
downtime: One discretionary slice, spent in the evening against five competing leads. This is the session where the time economy should first genuinely hurt.

scenes.title: Morning — The Sweep
scenes.description: Twelve walls of cicada stencils to paint over on Cannery Row, and no supervision. Every investigative action costs a wall off the docket. The deduction the whole chapter turns on — that the stencils are all at head height, on walls people stand in front of — has to be earned rather than given.

scenes.title: Noon — The Hall
scenes.description: A Directorate public information meeting at the Wharfside Institute. The party are there as escort, which means standing at the back in uniform being looked at. Satoru gives an honest account of a dishonest position; Kudo takes it apart; Rika asks whether anyone has actually measured the thing.

scenes.title: Evening — What To Do With It
scenes.description: Five leads, one slice. They can do one. Six players will want three. The choice is the scene, and which four they decline is the part worth recording.

scenes.title: Night — Cannery Row Again
scenes.description: A man having an argument with a spaniel that will not walk down forty feet of ordinary pavement. Delivered on the way to somewhere else, and then the session ends.

endOfEpisodeEffects: Whichever four evening leads were declined decay on their own schedule — the chandler will still be there next week, Kudo's mood will not.
If the bike-shed date was found, one player is holding an eleven-year-old demonstration anniversary that nobody else at the table knows about.
danglingThreads: Who has been re-stencilling the school bike shed, and who has been painting over it, for eleven years.
Shinobu Kudo: four months detained, not charged, not ill by the Directorate's own physicians.
Nobody has measured the agent. Rika noticed; the Directorate has not answered.
notes: dayRange is null on purpose: this sits well past Day 6, where the Contact Pool makes the calendar procedural, so which day it lands on is a running decision rather than an authored one.
